limitations: Clinical literature adjudication only. All main text, all twelve main page images, four static figures, full five-column Table1 and complete ten-page supplement personally read; Video1 not watched, so review remains incomplete.

Full review does not imply causal certainty: the authors frame RRP12 as candidate, explicitly allow spurious association for rare biallelic variants, and describe D.II.1 pathogenicity as highly uncertain.

A.II.2 age21 narrative versus16 Table1; B.II.1 onset6years versus infantile framing; C.II.1 onset63/None table versus anxiety20/tinnitus50 narrative; C.II.2 bipolar59, other table findings60, CT65. Those time points are kept separate.

Chinese c.2634T>G/p.F878L versus c.2334T>G/p.F778L conflict; main Figure2C c.1158C>T label versus c.1558C>T narrative. Supplement S2D/E447K and E477K elsewhere conflict. No transcript/genomic normalization inferred from a typographical majority.

Supplement p6 has conservation/model image with fibroblast caption; p9 has fibroblast images/mRNA/growth curves with conservation caption. Growth panel compares patient with mother only, despite main prose mentioning controls. Main Figure3 count quantification is A.II.2 only.

Supplement S2C axis says mRNA although caption describes protein; S2D has broken axis, unequal transcript overexpression, similar RRP12 and Myc protein signals; antibody-specificity controls do not establish normal variant function.

Supplement S4 RNA significance bracket is WT versus C.II.2 but caption says A.II.2. NOC3L protein reduction in A.II.2 is significant in caption/plot, although main describes minimal reduction. TableS3 AATK MetaRNN22.7999 is outside its usual0–1 scale, and RRP12 CADD27.8999 differs from main32; retain rather than silently fix.

Zebrafish images labeled day7 while text/curve show maximum survival6days; no calcification phenotype and no direct knockdown measurement. Published methods were read as evidence only; no wet-lab design or execution.
